newsitem.title: USA: Mazda to consolidate North American units.
newsitem.headline: Mazda to consolidate North American units.

text.p: Mazda Motor Corp said late Thursday that it plans to consolidate its North American operations, a move that would likely lead to a 25 percent reduction in its work force.
The company said that by the end of the year it plans to consolidate its five North American companies into two companies: one based in the United States and the other in Canada.
Mazda did not immediately return a telephone call seeking further comment and details.

The five North American companies now are Mazda Motor of America Inc, headquartered in Irvine, Calif.; Mazda (North America) Inc, headquartered in Flat Rock, Mich.; Mazda Research and Development of North America Inc, headquartered in Irvine, Calif.; Mazda Systems Services of North America Inc, Flat Rock, Mich.; and Mazda Canada Inc, headquartered in Toronto, Canada.

Richard Beattie, the president and chief executive of Mazda's North American operations, said in a statement that the "new streamlined organisation represents the first step in major restructuring of the way Mazda does business in North America and will lead to improved customer service and a much more competitive position in the U.S. and Canada."

The statement also quoted from a letter sent to employees, saying: "There's no way to sugarcoat this kind of news. These are difficult decisions that must be made if Mazda is to realise the potential it has to be a major player in North America."
Beattie said in the statement that he expects to slim down the workforce through attrition, layoffs and the elimination of some open positions.
Mazda is 33.4 percent owned by Ford Motor Co.
